doc.title: 68088_Wilbur B. Ware, Sr oral history interview

chapter: Back to Chicago and the road to jail and illness
title: Tuberculosis and Bellevue Hospital in 1963
summary: A friend takes him to Bellevue where TB is found, and he is sent to the Veterans Hospital at Castle Point.

story.theme_name: Illness, injury and the deaths of colleagues
story.community_name: Illness, injury and death among jazz musicians

blocks.x: this was about in '62; I was gigging, around, you know, just little gigs here and there. In 1963 I got so I couldn't go up stairs; I'd get out of breath, you know, I was coming down with TB. You know, I always believed that you had TB, you'd be spitting up blood, but it hadn't reached that stage, and (unintelligible) a lady friend of mine saw me during this time, "You don't look good; and said, 'come on, let me take you to Bellevue', and I said "Oh, I will go tomorrow", and she said, "No, I will go with you right now." And she said, "If they don't keep you you can come and stay at my apartment", you know. Just friendly, like, you know.

I went over there and the man said, "Oh!" and they rushed me upstairs. So she left me in Bellevue, and I stayed there, oh, a couple weeks. And then I was in there awhile, and he said, "You better?" and I say, "Yeah" and he said if I really didn't feel better to tell the contact man and they would send me upstate, you know, and get better treatment and be able to get an allotment check, or something like that.

So I said sure, and when the contact man got through, I told him I remember my army serial number, naturally, and a couple of weeks later, they sent me up to Castle Point, New York -- up around Newburgh... somewhere up in there. The Veterans Hospital. And when I got up there, oh, I was doing good; again, I had a chance to start eating right and getting my rest, and my TB was at the point where they caught it in time
